newsitem.title: FRANCE: Russia's Dubinin sees rouble policy continuing.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Dubinin sees rouble policy continuing.

text.p: Russia plans to continue its policy of regulating the exchange rate of the rouble, central bank head Sergei Dubinin said on Wednesday.
He also said that he expected economic growth to be at least flat next year after contracting in 1996.
Dubinin, speaking in Russian through a French interpreter at a bankers conference in Paris, said Russia wanted to avoid excessive fluctuations in the rouble.
"Exchange rate policy will be in line with what was done over the last two years, with a few small modifications," he said.
He later told Reuters Financial Television in an interview that the central bank would issue a decree before December 1 on regulating the exchange rate.
Dubinin reiterated that he expected inflation to come down to 10 to 12 percent per year next year from 22 to 24 percent this year.
The economy would improve after a shrinkage of around five percent in 1996.
"We hope to see a reversal in that trend in 1997... to obtain at least zero percent," he said, adding this would be mainly due to exports.
He said he wanted to see interest rates come down further.

Dubinin also said that the members of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) should take inspiration from western Europe and co-ordinate their exchange rate policies rather than falling into a currency war.
"We are more and more convinced that we must coordinate exchange rate policy," he said.
He noted that Europe was integrating its policies at different speeds for different countries.
"It will be the same for the CIS in the coordination of our exchange rate policies," he said.
